items.q: Why does Saylor call Bitcoin digital capital rather than money?
items.a: Fiat is **permissioned counterparty money** (~**7%/yr** bleed vs scarce desirables). **Bitcoin** is portable, unconfiscatable capital — buy what robots cannot print. Horizon: money not needed **≤4 years** (ideally 10). Forecast cited: ~**30%/yr** for ~20 years then ~20%.

items.q: How did ChatGPT supposedly help raise ~$15B?
items.a: **Don't outwork robots** — ask AI for what civilization has **never done**. MicroStrategy used ChatGPT to design Bitcoin-backed preferreds (STRK) and a variable-monthly-dividend preferred that traded near par — ~**$15B credit** sold.

items.q: Where should a young adult sit on the S-curve?
items.a: At the commercially viable **zero-to-one window** (digital intelligence / digital assets / "magic" products), not the diminishing-returns end (surgeon/lawyer/driver as default). Grow like a **chambered nautilus** — extend existing foundations, don't open 37 mediocre restaurants.

items.q: Why sell any BTC if the slogan is never sell?
items.a: To break the **"they can never sell / BTC dies if they sell"** short narrative and show dividends can be funded from BTC so equity need not be diluted forever. Treat the $15B line as **his telling** of the preferreds story.
